Name: OAuth 2.0 (Authorization Code + PKCE)
Strengths: Industry standard, decoupled IdP, no password handling
Common Pitfalls: Implicit flow (deprecated); leaking tokens in URL fragments
Notes: Always Authorization Code + PKCE for public clients; never Implicit (RFC 9700 'OAuth 2.0 Security BCP').

Name: OpenID Connect (OIDC)
Weaknesses: ID token vs access token confusion
Common Pitfalls: Trusting the access token as identity; always validate ID token
Keywords: oidc openid connect id token jwks
Notes: Cache JWKS with short TTL; never trust 'iss'/'aud' without validating both.

Name: JWT (JSON Web Token)
Weaknesses: Revocation is hard; size grows with claims
Common Pitfalls: Using 'alg: none'; not validating 'exp'/'aud'/'iss'; long TTLs
Notes: Prefer short TTL (5–15 min) + refresh tokens; use ES256/EdDSA over HS256 to enable key rotation.

Name: SAML 2.0
Strengths: Mature in enterprise, supported by every IdP
Notes: Use a battle-tested library; never hand-parse SAML; pair with SCIM for user lifecycle.

Name: mTLS (Mutual TLS)
Use Case: Service-to-service inside a mesh, B2B APIs, IoT
Strengths: Cryptographically strong identity, no shared secrets
Weaknesses: Cert lifecycle/rotation infra needed; harder to debug
Common Pitfalls: Long-lived certs; trusting any cert from a CA root
Keywords: mtls mutual tls x509 spire spiffe
Notes: Use SPIFFE/SPIRE or service-mesh CA (Istio/Linkerd) to automate short-lived cert rotation.

Name: API Keys
Use Case: Server-to-server, partner integrations, low-risk public APIs
Weaknesses: Hard to rotate; often leaked into Git/Slack
Notes: Hash & rotate, scope per integration, support quick revocation, monitor usage anomalies.

Name: HMAC request signing
Use Case: Webhook receivers, server-to-server APIs (AWS SigV4 style)
Strengths: Tamper-evident, no token replay if nonce included
Common Pitfalls: Forgetting to verify signature; using non-canonical request encoding
Notes: Include nonce + timestamp; reject requests outside ±5 min skew.

Name: Session cookies (server-side session)
Strengths: Easy to revoke, smallest surface, mature
Weaknesses: Cross-domain story is hard; CSRF must be addressed
Notes: Default to 'SameSite=Lax' + double-submit token for state-changing requests.

Name: Passkeys / WebAuthn
Weaknesses: Account recovery & cross-device UX still maturing
Common Pitfalls: Treating passkeys as 2FA only; bad fallback flows
Notes: Offer passkeys as primary login with password/OTP fallback; sync-fabric (iCloud/Google) handles device loss.

Name: Magic links / OTP email-SMS
Weaknesses: Email/SMS deliverability, SIM-swap risk for SMS
Common Pitfalls: Long-lived link tokens; reusing same OTP
Notes: Always single-use, ≤15 min TTL; rate-limit per identifier and per IP.

Name: RBAC (Role-Based Access Control)
Common Pitfalls: Hard-coding role names in app; missing audit
Notes: Externalise policy (Casbin/OPA/Cedar) instead of 'if user.role == admin' scattered everywhere.

Name: ABAC / ReBAC (PBAC)
Common Pitfalls: Treating ABAC as RBAC + tags; no caching of decisions
Keywords: abac rebac pbac opa cedar zanzibar
Notes: Open Policy Agent (Rego), AWS Cedar, AuthZed/SpiceDB (Zanzibar) are the production choices.

Name: SCIM 2.0
Use Case: Sync users/groups from IdP to your app
Common Pitfalls: Treating SCIM as auth (it's just provisioning)
Notes: Implement SCIM endpoints to land on enterprise procurement checklists.

Name: Service-account tokens / Workload identity
Use Case: Pod → cloud API auth without long-lived keys
Strengths: No static secrets; tied to workload identity
Common Pitfalls: Using long-lived AWS access keys in pods (instead of IRSA / Pod Identity)
Keywords: workload identity irsa pod identity gke wif
Notes: AWS: IRSA / EKS Pod Identity. GCP: Workload Identity Federation. Azure: Workload Identity.
